name: Le palier
camera: at the top of the stairs, facing north along the first-floor landing

setting.walls: ivory wallpaper with olive-green fern fronds, dark oak doors
setting.floor: polished oak boards with a long moss-green runner
setting.landmark: a huge arched window at the back with a carved bench, and a tall oak coat-and-hat tree with an umbrella stand
setting.light: daylight pouring through the big arched window
setting.style: S07 gentle storybook painterly 3.5/5 (one style for the whole Quartier de la Santé)

items.scene: A girl with her hair up touches the little NOOK ("NEWK") at the NAPE of her neck, where a cold raindrop from the skylight just landed.
A grandpa taps a tin CAN ("KAHN") off the runner with his walking CANE.
A toy CHEVY ("shuh-VEE") car has rolled into a girl's foot, and she sits on the bench rubbing her ANKLE.
A boy who bumped his head holds an ice pack to his TEMPLE, little stars still circling from the THUMP ("TAHNP").
A lady's towering HAIRSTYLE is so grand that a QUAIL ("kwah") nests in it with A FEW ("FEWR") tiny eggs.
A poet in a velvet beret reads a SONNET ("soh-NEHT") aloud while pressing the brass DOORBELL by the workshop door.
An OSTRICH ("OS-trich") strides along the landing carrying a huge white BONE in its beak.
A mouse with NERVES ("NEHR") of steel walks a tightrope stretched NEAR the ceiling, balancing a pencil.
A duck HAIRDRESSER QUACKS ("kwah") happily as she snips a poodle's FUR ("FUHR") into neat pompoms.
A jester, a merry FOOL ("foo"), ties a silk HEADSCARF under his chin while a LARK ("LAHR") hops on his shoulder.

prompt:
Gentle storybook painterly illustration, realism about 3.5/5, soft gouache-and-oil brushwork, warm-hearted and calm, natural NEUTRAL daylight with true colours, off-white whites, no orange, sepia, amber or golden cast, no pink or blue tint, clear readable figures with contact shadows on the floor, consistent eye-level perspective, 16:9 wide composition.
Scene: Le palier in the B17_cabinet building, first floor (landing). Camera: at the top of the stairs, facing north along the first-floor landing.
Setting: ivory wallpaper with olive-green fern fronds, dark oak doors; floor: polished oak boards with a long moss-green runner. Landmark: a huge arched window at the back with a carved bench, and a tall oak coat-and-hat tree with an umbrella stand. Light: daylight pouring through the big arched window. The room feels lived-in and real, with depth (never an empty white backdrop).
Paint these exits clearly as walkable openings: the banister and top steps going DOWN in the near left foreground (way to La salle d'attente); a narrow wooden stair climbing UP at the BACK LEFT (way to L'amphithéâtre); a dark oak door at the BACK CENTRE beside the window (way to L'atelier de la main); a tall oak door on the RIGHT wall (way to Le cabinet d'anatomie).
Characters and objects, each a separate, clearly spaced group, feminine-word groups on the left half and masculine-word groups on the right half:
- far left, middle distance: A girl with her hair up yelps as a cold raindrop from the skylight lands in the little NOOK at the NAPE of her neck.
- left, middle distance: A grandpa taps a tin CAN off the runner with his walking CANE.
- left, foreground: A toy CHEVY car has rolled into a girl's foot, and she sits on the bench rubbing her ANKLE.
- centre-left, middle distance: A boy who bumped his head holds an ice pack to his TEMPLE, little stars still circling from the THUMP.
- centre-left, foreground: A lady's towering HAIRSTYLE is so grand that a QUAIL nests in it with A FEW tiny eggs.
- centre, middle distance: A poet in a velvet beret reads a SONNET aloud while pressing the brass DOORBELL by the workshop door.
- centre-right, foreground: An OSTRICH strides along the landing carrying a huge white BONE in its beak.
- centre-right, middle distance: A mouse with NERVES of steel walks a tightrope stretched NEAR the ceiling, balancing a pencil.
- right, foreground: A duck HAIRDRESSER QUACKS happily as she snips a poodle's FUR into neat pompoms.
- right, middle distance: A jester, a merry FOOL, ties a silk HEADSCARF under his chin while a LARK hops on his shoulder.
Leave a blank light board for the room sign high on the back wall. No written words, letters, numbers or logos anywhere (signs and plaques are blank boards). No blood, no wounds, no needles in skin (syringes only as capped harmless props), no alcohol, no smoking, no religious symbols, no red-cross emblem. Nobody cropped by the image edge; keep every figure well inside the frame with a clear gap between figures. Figures stand on the floor or sit on real furniture, never floating or in rows behind a counter.
